fruitful line of inquiry, and never get back to it. Lets see if your Spot can take direction.

Jeffrey, 
All our scanners are down so the drawings are sent to you via fax. 
The concept is an abstraction of the coral stone tile flooring we have throughout our existing 
hardscape. 
The mad tile would be 4'x4' or 5'x5' and would be made out of the stamped concrete with the 
coral stone finish. 
Drawing A: Embedded in the tile would be real coral and shells. As in the real coral stone tile, I 
would like to abstract the creatures and forms of the sea in a large scale and scatter them 
throughout the road, large scale coral, starfish, etc. These would be mosaics done in crushed 
coral stone. 
Drawing B: In other areas, I thought we could do abstractions of shadows, done in black 
concrete, plants and birds, etc. 
Drawing C: What do you think about a sundial at the road convergence near the heipad? I'd like 
to do something bold and graphic here. 
Let me know what you think.

Intellectual judgment along with intellectual ability. The two don't always go hand-
in-hand. This is also a list of people who have a certain type of intelligence, but 
may not necessarily have social intelligence, i.e, they arc a bit awkward. 
Jay is incredibly skilled socially compared to some of the people on this list. Just fyi. I 
personally am not bothered by social awkwardness, but this is your thing, and you 
would like a good mix, and that is understandable. Criteria will just be different 
then. 
You brought up Jay. This is a good example. Jay does listen, and then tends to offer up his 
own views. I very much enjoy interacting with Jay, and he is a close friend, and 
although I may not always agree with him, he does always offer up ideas that are 
interesting and worth thinking about. That's why I put him on the list. He has a 
certain way he maps the world and he is also very well read and informed. This is 
not an argument about Jay, just why I put him on the list. I would also put Nathan 
in the same category as Jay. Doesn't listen much, pontificates, don't always agree 
with what he says, but he tends to say things that are provocative and interesting. 
He has an interesting way of mapping the world too, and is well read and 
informed. I enjoy bantering with both of them, and count them as real friends that 
I have known and hung out with for many years. 
Some of the names listed are titans of intellectual ego. Steven Wolfram being amongst the 
worst of them. Others are very shy and socially and fashion awkward, but are 
amongst the very brightest and informed that I know, and will run intellectual 
circles around some of the names on this list. 
I very much like the idea of your asking people on this list to contribute names of the ten 
"brightest" people that they know. This list would provide an excellent set of 
references. 
Please note, that although I have a diversity of thinkers, I have distinctly avoided people 
who map the world in a magical way, and would encourage us to avoid "magical 
thinkers."

On Apr 17, 2009, at 1:17 PM, Al seckel <
> wrote: 
Jeff, 
Good to talk to you this morning on this subject, as it is one I am entirely comfortable 
with. ;-) 
The list I sent you yesterday has the criteria of thinkers, out of the box. These are amongst 
the very brightest people that I know, where I enjoy listening to them, and they 
say insightful things along with a deep understanding of the subject matter. 
Intellectual judgment along with intellectual ability. The two don't always go 
hand-in-hand. This is also a list of people who have a certain type of intelligence, 
but may not necessarily have social intelligence, i.e, they are a bit awkward. 
Jay is incredibly skilled socially compared to some of the people on this list. Just fyi. I 
personally am not bothered by social awkwardness, but this is your thing, and 
you would like a good mix, and that is understandable. Criteria will just be 
different then. 
You brought up Jay. This is a good example. Jay does listen, and then tends to offer up his 
own views. I very much enjoy interacting with Jay, and he is a close friend, and 
although I may not always agree with him, he does always offer up ideas that are 
interesting and worth thinking about. That's why I put him on the list. He has a 
certain way he maps the world and he is also very well read and informed. This is 
not an argument about Jay, just why I put him on the list. I would also put 
Nathan in the same category as Jay. Doesn't listen much, pontificates, don't 
always agree with what he says, but he tends to say things that are provocative 
and interesting. He has an interesting way of mapping the world too, and is well 
read and informed. I enjoy bantering with both of them, and count them as real 
friends that I have known and hung out with for many years. 
Some of the names listed are titans of intellectual ego. Steven Wolfram being amongst the 
worst of them. Others are very shy and socially and fashion awkward, but are 
amongst the very brightest and informed that I know, and will run intellectual 
circles around some of the names on this list. 
I very much like the idea of your asking people on this list to contribute names of the ten 
"brightest" people that they know. This list would provide an excellent set of 
references. 
Please note, that although I have a diversity of thinkers, I have distinctly avoided people 
who map the world in a magical way, and would encourage us to avoid "magical 
thinkers."

inverter bus 
Jeffrey, 
this is what I have so far, 
the Facts: 
-Instrument inverter bus light is flickering during flight 
-normal system operation is "A" inverter (2500va) powers, "Main Inverter BUS", and Main inverter "bus" powers 
Instrument Inverter BUS with a back up of small E inverter (only 500va). 
-there is one relay that I see in the schematic that controls switch obgy for the MAIN INVERTER BUS to 
the INSTRUMENT INVERTER BUS, since its the INST INV BUS is flashing now, I think the culprit is the 
"INSTRUMENT BUS CONTROL RELAY" this is the only relay that comes between Main inverter bus power and 
the Instrument INV BUS, " A" inverter is powering the MAIN bus, plus powers INST INV BUS, with a back up 
power for INST INV BUS is "E" inverter, the only thing to cause this instrument bus to flash would be an A 
inverter problem, but that would cause the MAIN INVERTER BUS to flicker also, I'm only getting the 
INSTRUMENT BUS light flickering, so I think its the INSTRUMENT BUS CONTROL RELAY this time. 
Meridean Avionics and Gulfstream Tech agree with my logic so far,,, 
I plan to address this temporary item in Florida 
thanks 
Larry

Dear Mr Epstein, 
My old friend Phil Levine was kind enough to give me your email and the ok to 
write to you. (You may know my brother Sebastiano) 
I'm not sure if you remember this, but many years ago when Ed Tuttle was staying 
with you, he came to visit me on Hassel Island about a possible house design 
project, and then I took him up to see Patti Birch's antique furniture for you. 
Recently I joined the board of the St. Thomas Historical Trust. Our big focus 
this year is the Hassel Island Initiative. 
Our mission is to preserve the many cultural monuments that exist there, and to 
make them available to residents and visitors to enjoy. The rich maritime history 
needs to be shared with the public, and the National Park attractions can 
eventually be an important part of our tourism offering. 
My grand father Isidor Paiewonsky's father Isaac purchased Hassel Island back in 
the late 20's. Isidor and his brother Governor Ralph M. Paiewonsky gifted a large 
part of the Island to the National park and the territorial government in and 
around 1983. Unfortunately, little has been done by either entity in terms of 
preservation or creating public access. 
The Trust will soon be meeting with Governor deJongh in hope of his signing a 
budgetary appropriation that will enable the Trust to continue restoration work 
on key sites that are underway now. 
We are also seeking out benefactors with an interest in historic preservation 
who can help make Hassel Island become a vibrant National Park. 
I grew up on Hassel, and would love the opportunity to give you a guided tour, or 
myself and a fellow board member could make a short visual presentation at your 
convenience outlining our specific funding needs and what sites we are working on 
now. It would be an honor for us to get your support on this important community 
endeavor 
Anyway, my apologies in advance for such a lengthy email, but Phil said to give 
you an over view. I look forward to hearing from you. 
Kindest Regards, 
Filippo Cassinelli

Arafat Day, Eid & apt 
Hallo All! 
I'm always surprised over how "flexible" the dates of the holidays arc here. Since holidays depend 
on the sighting of the moon and other imaginary fairytales, the government always manages to put 
a holiday in conjunction with a weekend. 
This year they managed to pull a new holiday out of the sleeve, Arafat Day, and put it next to Eid 
so we got Mon - Thurs off. Most take Sun off and voila you have 10 days offl Work is not highly 
rated here. 
It's been a year since I moved in to my apt! I now found a gorgeous new apt and will move 1 Dec. 
It's a lot closer to campus, it's bigger, newer and did I mention gorgeous? Also cheaper and this 
puppy lands on $25,000 / year. 
I will send a kodakgallery link to pies. 
A bona fide moving company quoted $400 to disassemble, pack, move, unpack and re-assemble 
my furniture. A colleague said I was being ripped off, but for 2 guys + a truck to work all day, I 
would feel embarrassed to pay less. This is a 3rd world country alright. 
So I have barely managed to get the Internet and cable hooked up, and now the fun starts all over 
again! The *%*(*y&% phone company here is just incapable of finding a house... Every day it 
baffles me how stupid people here are. It's very much like that movie, Idiocracy... 
I finally learned how to distinguish between the Abu Dhabi side and the Dubai side of the border: 
The Abu Dhabi side has lights on both sides of the highway whereas the Dubai side can only 
afford lights on one side... 
Be well.

Dear Alexa, 
Dec 20 
Staley 
Thanks for writing. Your message is timely. I and my group at NYU are 
working on several projects in computational astrophysics, 
particularly focusing on relativistic gas dynamics and very recently 
including coupling to dynamical space times. We are very much 
starting to move into numerical relativity with an eye toward accurate 
inclusion of gas dynamics relevant for neutron star-black hole and 
neutron star-neutron star binaries. We are motivated by advanced LIGO 
which I'm sure you are aware is scheduled to be on line starting in 
2014 and is expected to detect double neutron star mergers to several 
100 Mpc distances at which the event rate should be sufficient to 
yield detections. 
A graduate student in my group has recently written an Einstein/hydro 
code in 1D to simulate black hole formation during collapse of massive 
stars. Our goal is to extend this code to 3D using efficient adaptive 
mesh refinement on massively parallel computers to simulate black hole 
mergers at very high resolution. 
I am on sabbatical at Harvard this coming semester. But I will stay 
in touch with the application process. Good luck with your 
application. 
Best Wishes, 
Andrew

east, possible at +57-6".
